thread:
Jules (Support): :rotating_light: AcmeOps reporting sudden 502/504s from hosted inference (guest tenant) — started ~08:12 UTC after a small auth service deploy. Customer says streaming requests fail mid-stream or return 502 with upstream reset. Example trace id: trace=0af3c9b2-7e

AcmeOps (Customer): hitting this on a few requests, sample curl below. Happens for long streaming embedding batches and some short chat sessions. We saw a spike to ~14% 502s for that tenant.

Jules (Support): curl sample from customer:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/guest/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"gpt-embed-1","inputs":["...large payload..."]}'
```

Sam (Eng-SRE): Looking. Can you attach the full request/response headers and the trace IDs? Also which region/edge?

Jules (Support): Attached headers from one failed request (sanitized):
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.example
:path: /v1/guest/invoke
content-length: 124589
authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**
accept-encoding: gzip
x-edge-region: eu-west-1
x-request-id: 0af3c9b2-7e
```
Customer says it correlates with a background auth token rotation event at 08:11:45 UTC.

Marta (Eng-Platform): Suspect h2 keepalive / connection pool exhaustion at the front door (Envoy) when auth upstream briefly slows. If upstream auth or billing responds slower, Envoy may drop streams and return 502/504. Can we get envoy stats for the edge instances serving that tenant (h2: MUX stream resets, connection_pool.*)? Also check keepalive settings and max concurrent streams per connection.

Sam (Eng-SRE): Pulling envoy admin snapshot now. Quick check shows increase in upstream connection failures and "stream_reset_by_downstream" counters around 08:12. Example admin query used:
```
curl -sS http://localhost:19000/stats | egrep "stream_reset|connection_pool|pending_requests"
```
Gives lines like:
```
cluster.auth-upstream.cluster_maintenance.connection_pool_stream_reset_by_downstream: 642
cluster.guest-backend.http2.pending_requests: 0
cluster.guest-backend.http2.connection_pool_rq_timeout: 18
```

Sam (Eng-SRE): Temporary mitigation ideas: 1) revert the auth deploy if that lines up with customer impact window, 2) increase envoy per-host connection pool settings to allow more concurrent h2 streams, 3) enable short-term circuit for heavy long-poll embedding paths to a fallback model variant. Which do we want to try first?

Jules (Support): Customer prefers a quick config workaround rather than rollback. Can we bump pool size and TTL and watch? They can also route that tenant to a different route if needed.

Marta (Eng-Platform): Will patch a canary config on a small subset of edge nodes (eu-west-1) to bump max concurrent streams to 200 and increase connection window. I'll post the canary diff. If success (502s drop <1%) we'll roll to the cluster.

infra-bot: Deploy triggered: edge-config-canary/eu-west-1 by Marta at 2024-11-13T08:40:12Z :gear:

Sam (Eng-SRE): After canary, initial telemetry looks promising — tenant 502 rate down from 14% -> 0.9% in 10 minutes. Still collecting traces for a full hour.

Jules (Support): Updated customer, they report immediate improvement. Keeping thread open for post-mortem notes. :thumbsup:
